First continue independent work that should take priority; decide whether to wait before choosing duration. Only call wait_agent for an unfinished necessary direct child result with no other higher-priority work. Apply this at every authorized delegation layer, including Implementer/Reviewer waiting for an Investigator Scanner; observe only direct dependencies. Prefer event-driven native wait_agent waiting over timed polling. First confirm the current Host's actual maximum, meaningful-event early return, user interruption and child notification capabilities; unconfirmed capabilities remain UNKNOWN. When meaningful-event early return and user interruption are confirmed and no dependency needs an interim decision, default to the supported 60-minute window (timeout_ms=3600000). This is a maximum waiting window, not a required execution duration; native completion wakes the parent early. Short historical averages must not force an earlier wake. If timed stage checks are needed or early return is unreliable, recommend 60 seconds for very short tasks, 10–60 minutes for ordinary tasks by work scale, and about 30 minutes for longer-task stage checks; reliable events without interim decisions still favor 60 minutes. Actual tool limits, explicit applicable higher-level duration limits, user interruption, recovery and urgent decisions take precedence; never bypass Host limits. Distinguish native terminal evidence from ordinary child messages and timeouts: messages and timeouts do not prove completion; exceptions do not fabricate terminal evidence and unproved status remains UNKNOWN. After timeout, reassess necessary direct dependencies and available independent work before any further wait; avoid infinite useless waits. A wake-only result needs one available exact native status check. Use a completed result directly without confirming the same completion again. Do not substitute sleep, add progress pollers, create per-child timed polling loops, heartbeat services or repeatedly wake models for unchanged state. Neither fixed 60 seconds nor fixed 60 minutes applies universally; windows are not execution deadlines. Executing children continue work; report only completion, key blockers, major discoveries or necessary upper-level decisions, never elapsed-time progress. Executors own local tests, builds, CI and external processes, using their tools' actual waiting capabilities rather than wait_agent parameters; independent closing owns final acceptance.
